bonus.text: In 2019, Australian Indigenous troupe Kuma Kaaru performed at Nauru’s Centenary Hall and brought audience members on stage to join a dance of bird-like movements and sounds.
For the 2024 Festival of Pacific Arts in Hawaii, the schedule gave Nauru 10 performance slots on eight days, at venues from the Festival Village Stage to Waikiki Beach Walk.
On the first Angam Day, in 1932, the Nauruan people reached 1,500. Districts lit beach bonfires and chiefs judged the biggest: Aiwo won, its flames blue from copper wire.
